Q: Pydantic agent - the agent tool/toolset decorator does not work on top of methods which have the runcontext A:

It sounds like you are trying to define your tools as class methods and then bind them to the agent via the decorator. That's the core of the problem.

(Note: A full example of your code would help clarify this.)

There are 2 ways to bind tools in PydanticAI:

  1. register the tool directly in Agent(..., tools=[...])

  2. decorate the tool with @<agent_name>.tool

Note: If you do both, you'll get a name collision. (UserError: Tool name conflicts with existing tool: 'xyz')

Why the decorator silently fails on a class method

When pydantic-ai sees @chat_agent.tool, it inspects the decorated function's signature and treats the first positional parameter as the RunContext slot (reference). On a class method, that first parameter is self, not your ctx: RunContext[Deps]. So either the registration breaks outright, or it registers a tool whose schema is wrong and the model never calls it. Either way, the tool effectively doesn't exist at runtime.

tools=[xyz, abc, tst] works for you because by the time you put those references in the list, you're either pulling them off an instance (self.xyz — bound, so self is gone from the signature) or they're already plain functions.

Fixes, in order of preference

  1. Move the tools to module-level functions: (not method)
def xyz(ctx: RunContext[Deps], qry: str) -> str:
    ...

def abc(ctx: RunContext[Deps]) -> str: ...
    ...

chat_agent = Agent(..., tools=[xyz, abc])

reference

  1. Keep them on a class but register bound methods via the constructor — pydantic-ai will see the right signature because self is already captured:
class ChatTools:
    def xyz(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], qry: str) -> str:
        ...
    def abc(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps]) -> str:
        ...

    # now register the tools
    tools = ChatTools()
    chat_agent = Agent(..., tools=[tools.xyz, tools.abc])
  1. Or, if you want the decorator pattern on a class, decorate after instantiation by calling agent.tool as a regular method:
tools = ChatTools()
chat_agent.tool(tools.xyz)
chat_agent.tool(tools.abc)

tools.xyz here is a bound method, so self is already applied and pydantic-ai sees (ctx, qry) — exactly what it expects.

Q: Error:java: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError com.sun.tools.javac.code.TypeTags when trying to run maven A:

TL;DR: use Lombok website to see which version of Lombok has support for which version of Java.

A bit longer story:

The question is formulated in a bit messy way, as it contains two distinct and unrelated points, however, the first one ("Release version 5 not supported") seems to be solved by the OP, while the second part: ``` Error:java: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError com.sun.tools.javac.code.TypeTags Error:java: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError ``` seems to be *the problem*, as indicated by the title of this question.

The problem is compiling Java code with a Java compiler whose version is higher than supported by the Lombok dependency version you're using. In other words, that version of Lombok can't read the bytecode generated by later versions of javac.

Use the latest version of org.projectlombok:lombok dependency, and if you want to see the explicit release note mentioning which Java support has been added in which version of Lombok, have a look at this page.

Q: Sigmoid output - can it be interpreted as probability? A:

A sigmoid function is not a probability density function (PDF), as it integrates to infinity. However, it corresponds to the cumulative probability function of the logistic distribution.

Regarding your interpretation of the results, even though the sigmoid is not a PDF, given that its values lie in the interval (0,1), you can still interpret them as a confidence index or similar. With that in mind, I would say that your first interpretation is the most appropriate one, although you are free to implement whichever classifier suits your purposes better.

Q: What is the purpose of PkgInfo in iOS? A:

The contents of the PkgInfo file are the 4-byte package type followed by the 4-byte signature of your application.

It comes from OS X, iOS does not require this file and you don't need to do anything with it.

See the following: Book: Programming IOS 6 By Matt Neuburg

Apple Docs: https://developer.apple.com/library/mac/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPRuntimeConfig/Articles/ConfigApplications.html
